Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

perfect adjective

also flawless, perfectly, perfection, nobody’s perfect

classical

Cic. Brut. 70: jam plānē perfecta (Lewis & Short, s.v. perficiō)
Cic. de Or. 1.59: ōrātōrem plēnum atque perfectum

perfectus, perfecta, perfectum

adjective

finished, complete, perfect

The participle of perficiō, “carry through, finish”: what has been brought to completion and lacks nothing.

Other words

  • absolūtus, absolūta, absolūtum — finished, complete in every part

    adjective · also used · classical · Cic. Off. 3.14: perfectum atque absolūtum officium (Lewis & Short, s.v. perficiō); Plin. Ep. 9.38 (M-O s.v. perfect)

    From absolvō, “finish” (of a picture or a book); often paired with perfectus. Pliny’s omnibus numerīs absolūtus is “perfect in every respect” (Morgan–Owens).

  • ad unguem factus — finished to a fingernail, perfectly polished

    phrase · also used · classical · Hor. S. 1.5.32 (Lewis & Short, s.v. unguis)

    A craftsman’s image: a joint smooth enough for the fingernail to pass over it without catching (Lewis & Short).

Examples

  • perfectum atque absolūtum officium

    a perfect and complete dutyCic. Off. 3.14 (Lewis & Short)

  • ad unguem factus homō

    a man polished to perfectionHor. S. 1.5.32 (Lewis & Short)

  • Nēmō perfectus est.

    Nobody’s perfect.composed

See also practice, correct.

Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. perfect.

Cicero and Horace quoted as Lewis & Short quotes them.
